name: Tenstorrent
desc: Designs AI accelerator chips, RISC-V processor IP and Galaxy AI servers for developers, enterprises and sovereign infrastructure.
capacity_detail: Series E of USD 1.5bn at a USD 6.2bn post-money valuation (Oct 2026)
markets: Sells worldwide to developers, enterprises and sovereign AI infrastructure; operates from Santa Clara, Austin, Toronto, Belgrade, Tokyo and Bangalore.

signals.raise: USD 1.5bn Series E at USD 6.2bn valuation (Oct 2026; https://tenstorrent.com/newsroom/tenstorrent-announces-series-e)

rationale: Freshly funded Nvidia challenger with offices on three continents; F1 offers global B2B visibility alongside rival compute brands already in the sport.

name: Retym
desc: Develops coherent DSP and networking chips for cloud and AI data-centre optical connectivity.
capacity_detail: USD 180M total funding, including USD 75M Series D led by Spark Capital (Mar 2025)
markets: Sells networking silicon to cloud and AI data-centre operators and optical equipment makers.
rationale: Young infrastructure-chip brand needing recognition with hyperscalers; F1 technology partnerships reach data-centre decision makers, but B2B fit is narrow.

name: Substrate
desc: Builds X-ray lithography tools and plans its own US foundry to manufacture advanced semiconductors domestically.
capacity_detail: Raised USD 100M in a round valuing the company at USD 1bn (Oct 2025)
markets: United States semiconductor manufacturing; aims to offer foundry services to chip designers.
rationale: Patriotic US-manufacturing story suits the US Grands Prix, but a pre-revenue foundry has little need for consumer-scale visibility yet.

name: Altera
desc: Designs field-programmable gate arrays, CPLDs and embedded system chips used in data centres, networks and industry.
ownership: private equity: Silver Lake (51%; Intel holds 49%)
capacity_detail: Intel sold 51% to Silver Lake in a deal valuing Altera at USD 8.75bn; FY2024 revenue USD 1.54bn (Apr 2025)
markets: Sells FPGAs, CPLDs, ASICs and embedded systems to electronics, communications and data-centre customers worldwide.

signals.ipo: Confidentially filed for a US IPO estimated to raise USD 2bn (Sep 2026; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Altera)

rationale: Newly independent chipmaker heading to IPO needs a standalone brand; F1 hosts AMD and Intel, its direct FPGA rivals' parents.

name: ZEISS Semiconductor Manufacturing Technology
desc: Develops and makes lithography optics, photomask systems and wafer inspection equipment for semiconductor manufacturing.
ownership: private: Carl Zeiss AG majority, ASML 24.9% minority
markets: Supplies lithography optics, photomask systems and wafer inspection tools to the global semiconductor manufacturing industry from nine locations.
rationale: German precision-engineering brand behind every advanced chip; F1 showcases precision and could support ZEISS group recruiting and prestige globally.

name: TRUMPF
desc: Family-owned maker of machine tools and industrial lasers, including the laser amplifiers that generate EUV light for chipmaking.
markets: Sells machine tools, lasers and power electronics worldwide; about half of staff in Germany, rest abroad.
rationale: Engineering brand selling to manufacturers worldwide; F1's engineering audience and B2B hospitality fit its machine-tool and laser customers.

name: EV Group
desc: Makes wafer bonding, nanoimprint and photolithography equipment and inspection systems for semiconductor and MEMS production.
markets: Austrian manufacturing with subsidiaries in the USA, Japan, Korea, Taiwan, Singapore and China.
rationale: Niche B2B equipment maker; F1 could serve customer hospitality in Asia and the US, but brand-awareness need is modest.

name: Semikron Danfoss
desc: Makes IGBT and thyristor power semiconductor modules used in electric drives, welding equipment, lifts and forklifts.
capacity_detail: Semikron revenue EUR 452.9M in 2020, before the 2022 merger with Danfoss Silicon Power
markets: Power modules sold through 24 subsidiaries worldwide for drives, industrial vehicles, welding and lift equipment.
rationale: Power electronics for EV inverters link directly to F1 hybrid power units and electrification messaging toward automotive customers.

name: JSR
desc: Japanese maker of photoresists and other electronic materials used in semiconductor lithography, plus life-science materials.
ownership: state fund: Japan Investment Corporation (JIC fund holds 89.72%)
capacity_detail: Consolidated revenue JPY 440.7bn in the year to March 2026 (about USD 2.9bn); delisted June 2024 after JIC take-private
markets: Supplies photoresists and multilayer materials to semiconductor manufacturers worldwide; world leader in lithography photoresists.
rationale: State-backed materials leader consolidating the industry; F1 could raise its profile with global chipmakers, though B2B materials rarely sponsor sport.

name: Nichia
desc: Japanese maker of LEDs, laser diodes, phosphors and battery materials, including pioneering blue-violet laser diodes.
capacity_detail: Consolidated net sales JPY 502.1bn in 2022 (about USD 3.8bn)
markets: Supplies LEDs and laser diodes to automotive, lighting, display and electronics makers worldwide.
rationale: Automotive LED supplier with large revenue; F1 lighting and automotive links could support its brand with carmakers, though it is historically low-profile.

name: Toshiba
desc: Japanese conglomerate making power semiconductors, storage devices, energy and infrastructure systems, taken private in December 2023.
ownership: private equity: Japan Industrial Partners consortium
markets: Sells semiconductors, storage, energy systems and infrastructure worldwide, especially Japan, Asia, the United States and Europe.
rationale: Famous global brand rebuilding after delisting; F1 could relaunch its technology image as rivals like Lenovo, HP and Dell already sponsor teams.

name: Q-CTRL
desc: Builds quantum control and error-suppression software and quantum navigation sensors for aircraft and autonomous vehicles.
capacity_detail: Series C of USD 290M led by Salesforce Ventures (Nov 2026)
markets: Serves finance, energy, autonomy and aerospace customers; expanding in Japan and globally.
rationale: New quantum unicorn scaling globally; F1 suits its navigation technology story and puts it beside IBM and Google-backed tech brands.

name: nEye
desc: Develops silicon-photonic optical circuit switching chips that connect GPUs and servers in AI data centres.
capacity_detail: Total funding USD 152M after USD 80M Series C led by Sutter Hill Ventures (Apr 2026)
markets: Targets AI data-centre operators and hyperscalers needing optical interconnects.
rationale: Early-stage interconnect supplier selling to a few hyperscalers; F1 visibility offers little near-term commercial return.

name: DEEPX
desc: Designs low-power edge AI inference chips, modules and software for robotics, factories, cities and mobility.
capacity_detail: Total equity raised USD 159M (latest USD 11M Series D-II, Oct 2026)
markets: Korea plus partnerships in Japan, EMEA via Avnet Silica, Taiwan's AAEON and China.
rationale: Physical-AI chip brand building global distribution; F1 robotics and automotive themes fit, but its marketing budget is likely small.

name: TsingMicro
desc: Chinese designer of reconfigurable AI computing chips, edge chips and AI servers for computing centres and industry.
capacity_detail: Total equity raised USD 294M+, including USD 280M+ Series C (Dec 2025)
markets: Chinese smart computing centres, finance, energy, education and healthcare customers.
rationale: Domestic Chinese AI-chip supplier; F1 offers little unless it seeks international expansion around the Shanghai Grand Prix.

name: ChipLink Power
industry: SiC and GaN automotive power chips
desc: Makes automotive-grade silicon carbide and gallium nitride power semiconductor chips and power modules.
capacity_detail: Total equity raised USD 290M+, from a USD 290M+ Series C (Nov 2026)
markets: Automotive and power-electronics manufacturers; markets not stated beyond the automotive sector.
rationale: Automotive power-chip supplier; F1 hybrid and electrification themes fit its EV-inverter customers, though its reach appears domestic.

name: NanoCoreChip
desc: Develops 3D compute-in-memory AI inference chips built on SRAM and DRAM architectures.
capacity_detail: Total equity raised USD 337M+, latest USD 140M+ Series C2 (Oct 2026)
markets: AI inference chips for data-centre and edge customers; markets not stated.
rationale: Well-funded AI-chip start-up with unclear international ambitions; F1 is a long shot until it sells abroad.

name: Geener
desc: Start-up that designs analog and mixed-signal semiconductor chips for electronics manufacturers.
capacity_detail: Total equity raised USD 158M+, latest USD 88M Series C (Sep 2026)
markets: Analog and mixed-signal chips for electronics makers; markets not stated.
rationale: Component supplier with little consumer-facing brand need; F1 relevance is very limited.

name: Anhui Changfei Advanced Semiconductor
desc: Chinese start-up developing and manufacturing silicon carbide power semiconductor chips for power-electronics applications.
capacity_detail: At least USD 672M equity raised, latest USD 140M+ Series A+ (Feb 2026)
markets: Power-electronics customers in China; export markets not stated on the pages found.
rationale: SiC power chips are central to EV powertrains; an F1 link could help win foreign carmaker customers, but it is domestically focused.
